data.description:
## Problem

`rebar attach-commits` is documented as the repair surface for a commit that landed
without a `rebar-ticket:` trailer. It records the SHA, reports success, and the SHA
appears in the ticket's `commits` field. The close gate still refuses — with the same
error that recommends the repair. The recorded attachment is never consulted by the
check that raises, so the documented repair path cannot satisfy the gate it is
documented to repair. That leaves `--force` as the only exit, which agents are
forbidden to use, so the ticket becomes unclosable without a human override.

Reported against nava-rebar 0.13.1 (Python 3.14.7, macOS) by a client project.

## Evidence

Reproduction:

```
mkdir repro && cd repro && git init -q . && rebar init
printf '[verify]\nrequire_completion_verification_for_close = true\n' > rebar.toml
echo x > feature.py && git add feature.py && git commit -qm initial

T=$(rebar create task "Repro" -o json | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['id'])")
rebar set-file-impact "$T" '[{"path":"feature.py","reason":"repro"}]'

echo "feature change" >> feature.py
git commit -aqm "Change feature.py with no rebar-ticket trailer"

rebar attach-commits "$T" "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
rebar transition "$T" open closed
```

`attach-commits` succeeds and the SHA is durably recorded:

```
commits attached to 9571-6339-e851-46e3: 1
commits: [{'sha': '81d77f334b6829092716a64f89cf1bdf6a62e076'}]
```

The close then fails, recommending the repair that was already applied:

```
Error: cannot close 9571-6339-e851-46e3: it records file_impact (a code change) but no
commit references it (nor any of its descendants). Add a 'rebar-ticket: 9571-6339-e851-46e3'
trailer to the commit that implements it, then retry (or override with --force="<reason>").
Completion verification cannot confirm the work landed without a referencing commit.
```

## Root cause

`_check_work_landed` (`src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py`, ~line 195) raises at
~line 226 based solely on `_referencing_commits`, which delegates to
`commit_impact.referencing_commits` (`src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py`,
~line 166). That function reads `git log --format=%H%x1f%B%x00` and nothing else, so it
can only ever observe trailers and leading subject tokens. An attached SHA is invisible
to it by construction.

`_attached_commit_shas` (`close_precheck.py`, ~line 247) — whose own docstring names it
"the `rebar attach-commits` repair surface" — has exactly ONE call site, ~line 327,
inside `_check_file_impact_vs_diff`. That function runs only AFTER line 226 has already
raised.

So the two commit sources are unioned for the DIFF check and are not unioned for the
EXISTENCE check. The asymmetry is the bug.

The MCP tool docstring (`src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py`, ~line 122) states the contract the
code does not implement:

> The repair path when a commit landed without a usable `rebar-ticket:` trailer:
> attaching the SHAs records a COMMITS event so the close gate can still tie the ticket
> to its change.

## Suggested fix

At `close_precheck.py` ~line 226, test the union rather than the scan alone, matching
what line 327 already does:

```python
if own_impact and not referencing and not _attached_commit_shas(accepted_ids, tracker, **view_kwargs):
```

The asymmetric git-error handling documented at `_check_file_impact_vs_diff` still
applies downstream, so an attached SHA that is absent from the local clone remains
skipped rather than blocking.

Note the alternative the reporter offers: if attaching is NOT meant to satisfy this
gate, then the error text and the tool docs must stop presenting `attach-commits` as the
repair for it. Either resolution closes the contradiction; shipping both texts unchanged
does not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A close whose only evidence is an attached SHA succeeds, where before it raised.
  Verified by a test that performs the reported reproduction — `set-file-impact`, a
  commit with NO trailer, `attach-commits`, then close — and asserts the close lands.
- [ ] That test FAILS if the union at the existence check is reverted to the scan alone,
  so it is a regression oracle rather than a restatement of current behaviour.
- [ ] An attached SHA that is absent from the local clone does not block the close, and
  does not crash it. Verified by a test attaching a SHA that no local object matches.
- [ ] A ticket with `file_impact` and NEITHER a referencing commit NOR an attached SHA
  still raises, with the existing message. Verified by an unchanged existing test, so
  the gate is not weakened into always passing.
- [ ] The error text and the `_mcp_writes.py` tool docstring agree with the shipped
  behaviour. Verified by reading both against the code path.

## Testing

```
python -m pytest tests/unit/test_close_precheck.py -p no:randomly -q
```
data.title: attach-commits records SHAs the close gate's existence check never reads, so its documented repair cannot satisfy that gate
